input.lead: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
input.summary: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
input.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

input.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
